notes: What the app gets wrong today. Each entry prints as KNOWN on every run and does not fail it. An entry that stops matching fails the run until it is taken off the list, so a fix is always noticed. The contrast entries are one per screen, theme and color pair, each with the ratio the app draws. The language entries are one per kind of word the API cannot send in Spanish yet, which stay until it does, and one per place the portal itself still draws English, which the build that fixes it takes off.

accepted.why: The person's name in the header runs to one line and ends in an ellipsis when there is no room. Accepted: the name is theirs to recognise at a glance, the avatar beside it is the way to their profile, and the whole name is on the Profile screen.
The role under the name runs to one line and ends in an ellipsis the same way, and for the same reason.

An unfinished report's title on Help runs to one line and ends in an ellipsis when there is no room, the way a name does. The stub serves the first form's title in Spanish from this build on, and the Spanish is longer.
The role under the name, in Spanish now, runs to one line and ends in an ellipsis the same way the English one does, and for the same reason.

failures.what: is a to-do item the API sent in English
failures.why: A to-do item and its instructions are written in English in the database and the API sends them as written. The API's build gives them Spanish and sends the language the request asks for.

failures.what: is a to-do zone the API sent in English
failures.why: A to-do item's zone is written in English in the database and sent as written, the same as the item.

failures.what: is a shift header the API sent in English
failures.why: A checklist's shift and block names are typed in English and sent as typed. Step 118 gives an item its own words in the request's language as display, and gives the headers none, so they stay English until the API sends them in Spanish too.

failures.what: is a supply the API sent in English
failures.why: A supply's name and its unit are written in English in the database and sent as written.

failures.what: is a notice the API sent in English
failures.why: An in-app notice is written by the API in English at the moment it is sent. The API's build writes it in the person's saved language.

failures.what: is an inspection item the API sent in English
failures.why: An inspection's name, its items and their zones are written in English in the database and sent as written.

failures.what: is a service the API sent in English
failures.why: A shift's service is written in English in the database and sent as written.

failures.what: is a site role the API sent in English
failures.why: A person's role at a site is typed by an admin, in English today, and sent as typed.

failures.what: is a shift name the API sent in English
failures.why: A shift's name is typed by an admin, in English today, and sent as typed.

failures.what: is a Help reply the API sent in English
failures.why: Help's replies, the fixed ones included, arrive from the API in English. The route already carries the language; the reply's language is the API's to change.

failures.what: is a refusal the API sent in English
failures.why: The API's refusals are English sentences on every route but the seven calls made before signing in, which Step 113 answers in the language the request asks for. The portal draws a refusal in Spanish when the table holds that exact sentence and every other one as sent, so a refusal from any other route stays English until the API sends the person's language there too.

failures.what: is a procedure name the API sent in English
failures.why: The procedures an answer cites are named the way the API writes them, in English. Their names are the API's to send in the person's language, with Help's replies. The suite draws one for the first time in this build.

failures.where: Help's answer as it is written: the first words before it is done, a bold phrase cut in two, and the finished answer drawn the way it always was
failures.check: the question goes to the streaming route with the body, the query and the headers the message route has always had
failures.why: Help sends every question to POST /api/agent/message and waits for the whole reply. The next commit sends the same body, query and headers to the streaming route.

failures.where: Help's answer as it is written: the first words before it is done, a bold phrase cut in two, and the finished answer drawn the way it always was
failures.check: the first words appear before the answer is done
failures.what: nothing was drawn while the answer was being written
failures.why: The screen reads the reply only once it is whole, so nothing shows until the last word is written. The next commit draws each piece as it arrives.

failures.where: Help's answer as it is written: the first words before it is done, a bold phrase cut in two, and the finished answer drawn the way it always was
failures.check: a bold phrase cut in two shows its words and never its marks
failures.why: Nothing is drawn while the answer is written, so there is no half-written bold to judge. The next commit draws the arriving answer without its marks.

failures.where: Help's answer as it is written: the first words before it is done, a bold phrase cut in two, and the finished answer drawn the way it always was
failures.check: a screen reader hears the answer once, when it is done
failures.why: Help has no live region, so a screen reader is never told an answer arrived. The next commit says the finished answer once, when it is done.

failures.where: Everything a streamed answer does today's answer does: a report it starts, a photo sent with the question, and an answer with no written procedure
failures.check: each question goes to the streaming route
failures.why: Help sends every question to POST /api/agent/message and waits for the whole reply. The next commit sends the same body, query and headers to the streaming route.

failures.where: An answer the API writes again: reset clears what was drawn, and the answer written after it is the one that stays
failures.check: the first try shows as it is written
failures.what: nothing was drawn while the first try was being written
failures.why: Nothing is drawn until the reply is whole, so the try the API throws away never shows and there is nothing for reset to clear. The next commit draws it, and clears it at reset.

failures.where: An answer the API writes again: reset clears what was drawn, and the answer written after it is the one that stays
failures.check: a screen reader hears only the answer that stays, once
failures.why: Help has no live region, so a screen reader is never told an answer arrived. The next commit says the finished answer once, when it is done.

failures.where: An answer that fails: turned away before it starts, and an error part way, each shown the way a refusal with its status always has been
failures.check: a question turned away is asked on the streaming route
failures.why: Help sends every question to POST /api/agent/message and waits for the whole reply. The next commit sends the same body, query and headers to the streaming route.

failures.where: An answer that fails: turned away before it starts, and an error part way, each shown the way a refusal with its status always has been
failures.check: Retry asks again and the answer comes
failures.why: Retry asks the message route again. The next commit asks the streaming route, the way the first send does.

failures.where: An answer that fails: turned away before it starts, and an error part way, each shown the way a refusal with its status always has been
failures.check: the answer shows as it is written until the error
failures.what: nothing was drawn while the answer was being written
failures.why: The screen reads the reply only once it is whole, so nothing shows until the last word is written. The next commit draws each piece as it arrives.

failures.where: A connection that drops once the answer has started: one line says so, the conversation is read back and the kept answer shows, and when that fails, Try again
failures.check: the answer shows as it is written until the connection drops
failures.what: nothing was drawn while the answer was being written
failures.why: The screen reads the reply only once it is whole, so nothing shows until the last word is written. The next commit draws each piece as it arrives.

failures.where: A connection that drops once the answer has started: one line says so, the conversation is read back and the kept answer shows, and when that fails, Try again
failures.check: a dropped connection reads the conversation back
failures.why: When the connection drops, the screen says the message was not sent and offers Retry, which asks the question again. It never reads the conversation back, where the API keeps the answer. The next commit does.

failures.where: A connection that drops once the answer has started: one line says so, the conversation is read back and the kept answer shows, and when that fails, Try again
failures.check: the kept answer shows in place of what was drawn, the way an answer always is
failures.why: The answer the API kept is never read back, so it never shows. The next commit reads it back and draws it.

failures.where: A connection that drops once the answer has started: one line says so, the conversation is read back and the kept answer shows, and when that fails, Try again
failures.check: a screen reader hears the kept answer once
failures.why: Help has no live region, so a screen reader is never told an answer arrived. The next commit says the finished answer once, when it is done.

failures.where: A connection that drops once the answer has started: one line says so, the conversation is read back and the kept answer shows, and when that fails, Try again
failures.check: one line says the connection dropped
failures.why: The screen has no line for a dropped connection. It says the message was not sent, which stops being true once the API has the question. The next commit adds the line, and the one after gives it its Spanish.

failures.where: A connection that drops once the answer has started: one line says so, the conversation is read back and the kept answer shows, and when that fails, Try again
failures.check: with no answer kept yet, Try again is offered
failures.why: The screen offers Retry, which asks the question again, and nothing that reads the kept answer back. The next commit offers Try again.

failures.where: A connection that drops once the answer has started: one line says so, the conversation is read back and the kept answer shows, and when that fails, Try again
failures.check: Try again reads the conversation back again and the kept answer shows
failures.why: There is no Try again to read the answer back. The next commit adds it.

failures.where: A connection that drops once the answer has started: one line says so, the conversation is read back and the kept answer shows, and when that fails, Try again
failures.check: when the conversation cannot be read back, the line and the refusal show with Try again
failures.why: The screen has no line for a dropped connection and never reads the conversation back. The next commit adds both, and the one after gives the line its Spanish.

failures.where: A connection that drops once the answer has started: one line says so, the conversation is read back and the kept answer shows, and when that fails, Try again
failures.check: Try again after a failed read shows the kept answer
failures.why: There is no Try again to read the answer back. The next commit adds it.
